note: Owner 2026-11-14: a research finding is built only with a 'keep' verdict here. exists = who already publishes this question's answer; gain = what our page adds that they do not. Write both before building a new finding; a finding that fails is cut, not polished (lib/research.py gain_ok).

/research/peak-month/.exists: USGS publishes each gauge's annual peaks as raw rows; no agency states which month a given river's yearly high usually comes in.
/research/peak-month/.gain: The usual peak month, average date and how tightly peaks cluster for every gauge on the site, in one table a reader can search by river.

/research/flood-stage-years/.exists: NWS publishes each forecast point's flood stages; USGS publishes annual peak stages; neither says how often a river reaches flood stage.
/research/flood-stage-years/.gain: The share of years each river's yearly peak reached minor flood stage, only where the USGS and NWS scales agree.

/research/water-temperature/.exists: USGS publishes daily water temperature series per gauge; no monthly summary a swimmer or angler can read.
/research/water-temperature/.gain: Each gauge's average water temperature by month, side by side, with the coldest and warmest in July.

/research/tides/.exists: NOAA plots observed water against predicted tide one station at a time.
/research/tides/.gain: Every station on the site side by side: how far the sea ran above or below its tide table over the last 3 days.

/research/lake-levels/.exists: Each agency (Corps, Reclamation, CDEC, TWDB) publishes its own lakes' figures on its own site.
/research/lake-levels/.gain: Small: the site's lakes in one table, each against its own agency's full mark with the basis named. Kept as a convenience page (owner 2026-11-14).

/research/world-rivers/.exists: PEGELONLINE, the Environment Agency and Water Survey of Canada each publish their own gauges.
/research/world-rivers/.gain: Small: low, normal or high counted country by country, each label's basis named. Kept as a convenience page (owner 2026-11-14).

/research/peak-change/.exists: USGS and EPA publish peak-flow trend studies on thousands of gauges.
/research/peak-change/.gain: None: 90 search-picked gauges cannot answer a national question better.

/research/100-year-floods/.exists: USGS and FEMA explain the 1% annual chance and its odds over a mortgage.
/research/100-year-floods/.gain: None: 20 gauges add no evidence to that.
